name: Kiyomizu
tagline: Touch the clay of Kyoto. Learn from third-generation masters.
prompt: A booking site for a small ceramics studio in Kyoto that runs wheel-throwing classes for travellers

spec.name: Kiyomizu
spec.world: At our secluded workshop in Higashiyama, Kyoto, Master Kenjiro Kondo (born 1961) guides just five guests per session. A 3-hour private wheel-throwing session costs ¥18,500 per person, which includes premium Shigaraki clay, glaze selection, and international shipping of your finished vessel (processed over 6 weeks). The current seasonal glaze is 'Higashiyama Moss', a deep, ash-speckled green inspired by the local temple gardens.

imagery.subject: Close-up of wet, spinning gray clay centering perfectly on an old iron kick-wheel, hands of the artisan covered in slick slip.
Sunlight streaming through dark wooden lattice windows onto five empty, pristine pottery wheels in a row inside a historic Kyoto townhouse.
A finished matcha bowl glazed in the signature 'Higashiyama Moss' green resting on a rough, dark slate surface next to dry cedar shavings.
Portrait of Master Kenjiro Kondo smiling warmly in a dark indigo samue, standing before a floor-to-ceiling drying shelf stacked with unfired tea bowls.

spec.summary: An intimate online reservation house for an exclusive five-wheel pottery studio in Higashiyama, Kyoto, offering meditative, English-guided ceramic masterclasses for discerning travelers.
spec.tagline: Touch the clay of Kyoto. Learn from third-generation masters.
spec.audience: Cultured global travelers, design-focused couples, and art collectors seeking slow, authentic craft experiences in Japan.

directions.why: It honors the deep heritage of Kyoto master craftsmen, elevating a holiday activity into a serious, high-end cultural pilgrimage.
directions.twist: Using a palette inspired strictly by raw clay states (wet gray, unfired slip, and dark charcoal) with generous, quiet spacing that mimics the silence of an empty zazen temple hall.

directions.why: Pottery is inherently of the earth, and an organic design connects the user directly to the physical elements of water, mud, and wood.
directions.twist: An asymmetric, natural layout using rough-edged torn-paper textures, rich warm ochre backgrounds, and cursive hand-brushed calligraphic annotations.

directions.why: For design-conscious travelers, treating the pottery studio like a contemporary modern art archive makes the experience feel highly curated.
directions.twist: A precise, fine-line layout featuring architectural blueprint-style diagrams of ceramic cross-sections and raw kiln temperature readings.

spec.heroObject: An exquisite, single-shot film photograph of a raw, wet clay vase rising slowly between the weathered, clay-stained hands of Master Kenjiro Kondo.

Higashiyama, Kyoto · Established 1934

Kyoto is not seen;
it is shaped by hand.

At our secluded workshop, Master Kenjiro Kondo guides just five guests per session. Touch raw Shigaraki clay, hear the rhythmic spin of the wooden kick-wheel, and capture the quiet spirit of Kyoto craft.

01 // THE KICK-WHEEL IN MOTION Master Kenjiro Kondo, born 1961.
Three Generations of Clay

“The clay listens to your posture. If your mind is hurried, the vessel will lean.”

For nearly a century, our family has tended to the clay deposits of Shigaraki, refining earth into vessels that preserve the warmth of their maker's hands. We believe that true luxury lies in absolute presence.

Our Higashiyama studio offers a meditative, slow-paced sanctuary from the modern world. Here, we invite you to disconnect from the digital noise, plunge your hands into wet earth, and feel the friction of natural elements.

Kiyomizu
The Studio The Class Reserve
Reserve a Wheel
The Three-Hour Anatomy

A meditative dialog with wet earth.

In our secluded Higashiyama workshop, Master Kenjiro Kondo guides just five guests per session. Under his watchful instruction, you will learn the quiet language of centering, pulling, and finishing raw Shigaraki clay.

01 · CENTERING (30 MIN)

Finding the Axis

Before the clay can rise, it must find perfect stillness. Under Master Kondo's hands-on guidance, you will apply steady pressure to the spinning mound on the iron kick-wheel, learning to quiet the tremors of your own posture.

02 · PULLING (60 MIN)

Giving Form to Water

Drawing up the walls of your vessel with slow, rhythmic breathing. You will feel the clay swell and rise between your fingers—balancing wall thickness, managing centrifugal force, and shaping the lip of your future chawan or vase.

03 · TRIMMING (40 MIN)

The Kodai Foot

Using traditional Japanese iron scrapers to carve the base of your vessel. This step defines the silhouette, revealing the coarse texture of the raw Shigaraki clay underneath and forming the classic ring foot.

04 · GLAZING & SIGNATURE

Selecting the Vessel's Cloak

Select from five signature glazes mixed from regional wood ash and local minerals, including our seasonal ‘Higashiyama Moss’. Master Kondo will personally fire your piece in our traditional kiln over a 6-week period.

INTERNATIONAL DELIVERY

Premium worldwide shipping via air courier. Hand-packed and delivered safely to the USA, UK, Singapore, and Europe within 42 days.

TUITION DETAILS

¥18,500 per artisan. All raw materials, tools, post-processing glazes, firing, and wooden storage box (Tomobako) are fully included.

Active Season Glaze Higashiyama Moss · No. 04

* Each piece reacts uniquely to the heat gradients inside Master Kondo's wood-fired kiln, guaranteeing that no two finished vessels ever share the exact same surface coloration.

The Studio Space

An oasis of silent concentration.

Built inside a restored 19th-century townhouse (machiya) in Higashiyama, Kiyomizu Studio filters out the rush of modern travel. Here, under soft afternoon light streaming through dark wooden lattices, you will find four empty iron kick-wheels and the aroma of wet clay waiting for your touch.
